newsitem.title: USA: White House disagrees with CBO deficit forecast.
newsitem.headline: White House disagrees with CBO deficit forecast.

text.p: White House spokesman Mike McCurry said on Thursday he would "respectfully disagree" with estimates by the Congressional Budget Office that President Bill Clinton's new budget would yield a $50 billion deficit in 2002 instead of the $17-billion surplus predicted by the administration.

"We respectfully disagree," McCurry said in his daily briefing. "We would note that over the last four years the projections of our own Office of Management and Budget have been more 'on the money' than alternative economic assumptions and forecasts."
But McCurry quickly took a conciliatory tone, saying that the environment in which this year's budget is likely to be negotiated is far less contentious than in years past.

"The environment in which the budget issue is clearly going to be dealt with now is ... more amicable," he said. "We're not into that kind of back and forth as we were a year ago or two years ago. We're in a different mode of operation now, with both parties working to finish the job of balancing the budget."

CBO Director June O'Neill told the House Budget Committee on Thursday that Clinton's budget proposal would yield a $50 billion deficit in 2002. The administration predicts the budget would lead to a $17 billion surplus that year.
